scope: Typed public Rust SDK subscribe/unsubscribe and owned signed preparation/result pairing, including actual two-SDK-peer decoded audio/video, routing/no-op/replay and captured recording recovery. Local macOS arm64 functional scope; not full SDK or complete both-ends journey qualification.
implementation: Connection.subscribe has explicit Stream or Participant/kinds selectors; unsubscribe has explicit Stream IDs. Native revision, original operation ID, opaque extensions and selector order survive uncertainty and recovery. Distinct typed operation kinds preserve historical result identity.

Native stream result records original command, expected/resulting revision, Connection generation, resources_changed and optional captured bindings. A missing concurrent capture is null, never an invented empty set. Shared protocol validation bounds positive counters and native port identities.

Owned selection reoffers preserve local publication, restrict new ports to receiving declared formats and reserve positive unique native handles, including private data handles. Matching completed captures adopt local parameters; unknown/failed/interrupted paths preserve identity. Route-only/no-op receipts cannot rewind newer local revisions.

Native media queues can add/remove selected receive bindings while preserving unrelated queues and exposing discarded packets through counters/gaps. Saved observations never acquire foreign media custody. HTTP/OpenAPI reference documents captured selection outcomes.

Worker validates the OperationUpdated payload logical operation ID and bounded operation revision before applying any selection capture, independently of signed envelope/transport correlation. A signed foreign payload ID without ACK must immediately refuse Protocol.

client.scope: Complete client suite, including malformed signed reoffers/results, added video/data receives, route-only/no-op/stale observations, dropped caller/unknown recovery, explicit extension preservation and failed/unavailable captures.

protocol.scope: Complete protocol unit suite. New capture checks distinguish empty/null/missing metadata and reject aliased/foreign ports and incompatible counters/kinds.

store.scope: Targeted native_stream_authority group; not the whole Store suite.

production.scope: Two new both-ends SDK functions under EdDSA and ES256, eight existing SDK functions selected without repeating the new two, four original canonical future-selector functions, one native handle-custody function and two selector-policy/data refusal functions. No default/full-suite or performance claim.
behaviors: Both source and receiver use owned public Rust SDK Connections. Actual received PCMU and VP8 are independently decoded with FFmpeg; video unsubscribe preserves decoded audio and produces no video while the source keeps sending. Resubscription restores video without new native resources, and repeated unsubscribe is a no-op with the original revision.

Original selection adds receive resources only after signed same-root preparation and matching captured completion. Historical saved-reference reads and original-ID replay return revision2 after current local routing advances4, without rewinding parameters or repeating the one native effect. Fresh-client recovery observes the same receipt without physical media custody.

A controlled completion-journal failure leaves original local parameters in place after confirmation. Another unsettled selection refuses locally with zero operation rows. Removing the trigger records the captured original commit; actual decoded media and one effect/attempt prove no repeated native mutation.

Existing SDK lifecycle/membership/Session/metadata/native controls and codec media regression functions pass. Original future-publication/reconciliation, native handle isolation and heterogeneous selector/disjoint-data refusal functions pass against the new captured Store result shape.
